comments.text: Growing up, my dumb dad wanted me to be with teachers that assigned a lot of homework that I have to bring it home with to complete. He never showed interest that my senses were already done when it came to academic materials. Having autism, I never did well in schools because of the teachers and the other students mostly, The only academic subject I showed highest interest was Math & Algebra.  Literature, social studies, and science were mostly impossible for me because of way too much information being too abstract to understand; my rejected abstract information. I believe that homework should not be assigned at all!

comments.text: I believe we need to go back to the Covid type school where school is done online with a teacher but can be done remotely. It forces parents to control their kids behavior in real time, they don’t learn each others bad behaviors, and gets the parents a little more involved with the kids education. It also takes away the “school daycare syndrome” for parents who don’t wanna deal with their kids and are grateful that their kids aren’t “around”. Birth control too as younger people get to see this and maybe not be so loose on “having kids for the wrong reasons” bc they’ll see that education is truly a village for the kids. Also the government needs to sit down and shut up when it comes to education. The power to discipline and educate our kids completely and correctly needs to come back where it should be, the parents and teachers. We are the ones raising and educating these kids we are on the front lines, so why is the government putting their noses where it truly does not belong.

comments.author: @turkrudnab
comments.text: I am a college history professor. Yesterday I wasted several hours with my department chair (who was very supportive), two disruptive students AND their parents. I had kicked the students out class. Instead of correcting their children, these parents came with their kids to the disciplinary hearing to defend their behavior. In our state, all college students despite their age are legally considered adults and parents are not allowed to advocate for them. They can be present, listen, and be supportive but that is it. That these spoiled, entitled young people have to have mommy and daddy with them (in college!) speaks volumes. These poor kids are stunted emotionally and intellectually and THAT is their parents' fault. NOT teachers. BTW, this is happening more and more often to me and my colleagues.
